findings.summary: execute_final_review_mutations applies acceptance commands cumulatively: _target_red re-reads the already-mutated file for each argv, so the 2nd+ frozen acceptance command deletes the wrong line and the target's red/green fact is unsound. This repo's own dd-acceptance has two commands, so it fires on every target; an uncovered call site can be recorded red and pass the gate -- the exact miss obligation 5 exists to catch. FROZEN_ACCEPTANCE in the test file has one command, so the frozen acceptance cannot see it.

Mechanical enumeration applies no source-language filter: any added line in any non-test file outside .dev-dispatch/.dd-evidence matching `name(` becomes a target -- Markdown prose, PromQL such as sum(rate(...)) in deploy/prometheus/*.yml, shell function definitions in scripts/*.sh. Deleting such a line can never turn the frozen acceptance red, so all_red is false and _with_final_review_mutations returns GATE_REJECT/MUTATION_TARGET_NOT_RED. build_pipeline arms the gate by default, so ordinary tickets touching docs or config are auto-rejected. Spec 54.1 names over-enumeration as a refusal condition; the dev_repo fixture is Python-only and covers none of this.

_drop_worktree discards the return code of `git worktree remove --force` and suppresses the rmdir OSError, so a failed cleanup silently leaves the one-shot copy registered in the subject repo's shared git dir while the receipt still reports subject_workspace_writes: 0.

handle_dd_awaiting_gate_wake is imported by nothing outside fleet_graph.self_gate -- no scheduler, CLI entry point, or MCP tool reaches it; scheduler/wake.py emits the dd_awaiting_gate fact but nothing routes it into the six-duty gate. Recorded as a note, matching the continuous review and the spec's own lineage text, which adjudicates the runner.py wiring as correct and locates the prior defect in the engine-side mechanism.

The instructed mechanical product-consistency check (git diff between implementation_subject_commit and subject_commit excluding .dev-dispatch) was not executed: this reviewer has only file-inspection tools and no shell or Git access. The review was performed against the checked-out product tree in the worktree; no product-file discrepancy was observed there, but the diff itself was not run.
